mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of months where PAYEMS increases month-over-month, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that supports economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of months where UNRATE < 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and GDP growth (GDPC1) is declining, the S&P 500 tends to produce negative 20-day returns due to heightened recession risks and reduced equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising and GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5%
failure_condition: In more than 40% of months where FEDFUNDS is rising and GDPC1 growth rate is negative, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation and monetary tightening cycles (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS rising), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns due to reduced real interest rates and heightened recession risks.
regime_hint: high inflation and monetary tightening cycle
failure_condition: In more than 40% of high inflation and monetary tightening cycles (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS rising), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand for residential construction, which is a leading indicator of economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of months where HOUST increases, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) below 100 signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of months where INDPRO < 100, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: When both consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) are increasing month-over-month, it indicates robust consumer demand and housing market strength, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of months where both RSAFS and HOUST increase, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which is a leading indicator of corporate profit growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of months where INDPRO increases, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns.
